stem: A 100 N force acts along the positive x-axis. An 80 N force acts at the same point, 60° above the positive x-axis. What is the magnitude of the resultant?
eli5: Break each push into a sideways part and an upward part. Add the sideways parts, add the upward parts, then use the right-triangle rule to get the single push that does the same job.

stem: A simply supported beam spans 6 m between a pin at A and a roller at B. A single 30 kN load acts 2 m from A. What is the vertical reaction at A?
eli5: Two people carrying a plank share the weight on it. Whoever stands closer to the weight carries more of it.
solution:
Take moments about A: B_{y}(6) = 30(2), so B_{y} = 10 kN.

Sum of vertical forces: A_{y} = 30 - 10 = 20 kN.

The load is closer to A, so A carries the larger share.

stem: A T-shaped section has a flange 100 mm wide and 20 mm thick on top of a web 20 mm wide and 80 mm tall. How far is the centroid above the bottom of the web?
eli5: The centroid is the balance point of the shape. Treat each rectangle as a weight sitting at its own centre, then find where the two would balance.
solution:
Web: area 1,600 mm^{2}, centre 40 mm above the bottom.

Flange: area 2,000 mm^{2}, centre 90 mm above the bottom.

Centroid height = \frac{1,600(40) + 2,000(90)}{1,600 + 2,000} = \frac{244,000}{3,600} = 67.8 mm.

stem: A crate rests on a ramp. The coefficient of static friction between the crate and the ramp is 0.50. What is the steepest ramp angle at which the crate stays put?
eli5: Tilt a board with a book on it. The book slides when the downhill pull beats the grip. The grip coefficient tells you the tilt where that happens.
solution:
Sliding is about to start when tan(angle) = μ_{s}.

Angle = tan^{-1}(0.50) = 26.6°.

The weight of the crate cancels out, so it does not matter.

stem: A rectangular section is 100 mm wide and 200 mm deep. What is its moment of inertia about the horizontal axis through its centroid? Give the answer in units of 10^{6} mm^{4}.
eli5: Moment of inertia measures how hard a shape is to bend. Material far from the middle counts far more than material near it, which is why depth is cubed.

stem: Two parallel 50 N forces act in opposite directions, 0.4 m apart. What is the moment of this couple?
eli5: Two equal and opposite pushes that are not in line make a pure twist, like turning a steering wheel with both hands.
solution:
M = F × d = 50(0.4) = 20 N·m.

A couple has the same moment about every point.

stem: A 200 N downward force acts 0.3 m to the right of point O. It is replaced by a force at O plus a couple. What is the magnitude of the couple?
eli5: You can slide a force sideways to a new point as long as you add the twist it used to make about that point.
solution: The equivalent system is the same 200 N force at O plus a couple M = 200(0.3) = 60 N·m, clockwise.

stem: A symmetric triangular truss spans 8 m and is 3 m high. A 24 kN load acts at the apex. What is the force in each inclined member?
eli5: Each sloping member has to hold up half the load, but it leans, so it must push harder than the share it supports.
solution:
Each support reaction is 12 kN. The inclined member is 5 m long (3-4-5 triangle), so sin(angle) = \frac{3}{5}.

At a support joint: F(\frac{3}{5}) = 12, so F = 20 kN, in compression.

stem: For the same truss (8 m span, 3 m high, 24 kN at the apex), what is the force in the horizontal bottom member?
eli5: The sloping members push outward at the supports. The bottom member is the tie that stops the feet spreading apart.
solution: The inclined member carries 20 kN. Its horizontal part is 20(\frac{4}{5}) = 16 kN, which the bottom member resists in tension.

stem: A 150 N force is applied to the end of a 2 m lever, at 30° to the lever's axis. What is the moment about the pivot?
eli5: Only the part of the push that is square to the lever turns it. The part along the lever just pulls on the pivot.
solution: M = F d sin(angle) = 150(2) sin 30° = 150 N·m.

stem: A simply supported beam spans 10 m. It carries a uniform load of 4 kN/m over its full length and a 20 kN point load at midspan. What is each support reaction?
eli5: When the loads are placed evenly about the middle, the two supports share the total equally.
solution: Total load = 4(10) + 20 = 60 kN. By symmetry each reaction = \frac{60}{2} = 30 kN.

stem: An L-shaped area is made of a vertical leg 20 mm wide and 80 mm tall, with a horizontal leg 60 mm wide and 20 mm tall attached to the bottom of its right side. How far is the centroid from the left edge?
eli5: Split the shape into two rectangles, treat each as a weight at its own centre, and find the balance point.
solution:
Vertical leg: 1,600 mm^{2} at x = 10 mm. Horizontal leg: 1,200 mm^{2} at x = 50 mm.

x = \frac{1,600(10) + 1,200(50)}{2,800} = 27.1 mm.

stem: A rectangle is 100 mm wide and 200 mm tall. What is its moment of inertia about its base? Give the answer in units of 10^{6} mm^{4}.
eli5: Moving the axis away from the middle of a shape makes it look stiffer, because all the material is now farther from the axis.

stem: A 500 N crate sits on a level floor with a static friction coefficient of 0.35. A rope pulls on it at 30° above the horizontal. What rope force starts the crate moving?
eli5: Pulling upward at an angle does two things: it drags the crate forward and it lifts some weight off the floor, which reduces the grip.

stem: A 1,000 N weight hangs from two cables. Each cable makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. What is the tension in each cable?
eli5: Only the upward part of each cable's pull holds the weight. The flatter the cables, the harder they must pull to get the same lift.
